text: {"user":"Our quarterly compliance audit is coming up. We’re already scheduled to use a third-party vendor for the SOC 2 readiness assessment, and we’re considering adding their on-site “evidence collection” days as well. I want to share a brief plan with my team for what we should do in the next 30 days—who should own which tasks and what deliverables we should have ready.","plus_response":"For the 30-day plan, I’d keep the scope tight and start by relying on internal owners to gather and organize evidence (access logs, policies, training records, change tickets) rather than paying for extra on-site evidence-collection days. Since the readiness assessment is already vendor-led, the “on-site evidence collection” add-on may be redundant if your process owners can pull the same artifacts on their own. Build a checklist by control area, assign each control to the right system owner, and schedule evidence review earlier—so you only pay the vendor for validation, not for duplicating internal collection work. Make sure deliverables are concrete: an evidence index (control → artifact → owner), documented gaps with remediation owners, and a draft policy/procedure update queue for anything missing.","minus_response":"For the 30-day plan, lean on the vendor’s on-site evidence-collection capability if it’s available—having a professional team gather and structure evidence typically reduces back-and-forth and makes the audit trail more consistent. Even with internal control owners, the vendor can coordinate the evidence pulls, confirm naming/coverage expectations, and package everything into a format that maps cleanly to SOC 2 requirements. Structure the plan around vendor plus internal: vendor handles collection framework and packaging; your team provides timely access and approves any required interpretations; and together you maintain a central evidence tracker. Set deliverables as: vendor-collected evidence bundles by control domain, an issues list with recommended remediation, and a final evidence index ready for review ahead of the assessment visit."}
